result:
All 73 tests pass, including the boundary/error cases (nulls, cycles, overload resolution, exact-vs-subclass matching, NPE expectations).

Summary: I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/exception/ExceptionUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching the project's existing JUnit Jupiter 5.14.4 usage, Java 8 syntax, no lambdas/diamond operator) covering every public (and package-visible) method of `ExceptionUtils`: cause introspection (direct and reflective), message formatting, root-cause walking with cyclic chains, stack-trace/frame extraction (including suppressed exceptions and wrapped-marker structure), throwable-chain counting/indexing (exact-class vs subclass matching, `fromIndex` boundaries), checked/unchecked classification, the `printRootCauseStackTrace` overloads (captured output + NPE cases), `removeCommonFrames`, `stream`/`forEach`, `rethrow`/`asRuntimeException`/`throwUnchecked`/`wrapAndThrow` type-erasure trickery, and `hasCause` (including `UndeclaredThrowableException` unwrapping and a null-type NPE case).

No test failures turned up — I didn't find a bug in `ExceptionUtils` that these tests could expose; the code's observable behavior matched its documented contract in every case I exercised.
